farming.title: Lotus Farming Guide
farming.description: Comprehensive guide to lotus farming techniques, from pond preparation to harvest.

items.title: Pond Preparation
items.description: Prepare a pond or container with 15-30 cm of rich, loamy soil. Water depth should be 30-60 cm above the soil.
items.tips: Use clay-heavy soil that won't float away. Avoid sandy or rocky substrate.

items.title: Tuber Selection
items.description: Choose healthy rhizomes with at least two growth nodes. Look for firm, unblemished tubers.
items.tips: Purchase from reputable nurseries. Avoid tubers with mold or soft spots.

items.title: Planting
items.description: Place tubers horizontally in the mud with growing tips pointing slightly upward. Cover lightly with soil.
items.tips: Plant in spring when water temperature reaches 15°C. Space plants 60-90 cm apart.

items.title: Water Management
items.description: Maintain consistent water levels. Lotus prefers still or slow-moving warm water.
items.tips: Use a float valve for consistent levels. Avoid strong currents or fountains.

items.title: Fertilization
items.description: Apply aquatic plant fertilizer tablets monthly during the growing season.
items.tips: Push tablets into the soil near roots. Avoid liquid fertilizers that promote algae.

items.title: Pest Control
items.description: Watch for aphids, spider mites, and lotus leaf beetles. Use organic methods when possible.
items.tips: Introduce beneficial insects. Remove affected leaves promptly.

items.title: Harvesting Flowers
items.description: Cut stems early morning when flowers are just opening. Leave at least 10 cm of stem above water.
items.tips: Use clean, sharp shears. Harvest every 2-3 days during peak bloom.

items.title: Root Harvest
items.description: Harvest lotus roots in late autumn after foliage dies back. Carefully dig rhizomes from the mud.
items.tips: Use water pressure to loosen soil around roots. Handle gently to avoid breaking.

faqs.title: Lotus Flower FAQs
faqs.description: Frequently asked questions about lotus flowers.

items.question: What is the difference between a lotus and a water lily?
items.answer: Lotus (Nelumbo) and water lilies (Nymphaea) are often confused but belong to different families. Lotus leaves and flowers rise above the water on tall stems, while water lily leaves and flowers typically float on the surface. Lotus leaves are round and cupped, while water lily leaves have a slit.

items.question: Can I grow lotus in a container?
items.answer: Yes! Dwarf and miniature lotus varieties are excellent for container growing. Use a wide, shallow container (at least 40 cm diameter) without drainage holes. Fill with heavy garden soil, plant the tuber, and cover with 10-15 cm of water. Place in full sun for at least 6 hours daily.

items.question: How long do lotus flowers bloom?
items.answer: Individual lotus flowers last 3-4 days. They open in the morning and close in the afternoon. The overall blooming season lasts from mid-summer through early fall, with peak bloom in July-August in the Northern Hemisphere.

items.question: Are all parts of the lotus edible?
items.answer: Yes, almost every part of the lotus plant is edible: roots (rhizomes), seeds, young leaves, stems, and even flower petals. Lotus root is the most commonly consumed part, widely used in Asian cuisines for its crisp texture and mild flavor.

items.question: What does the lotus flower symbolize?
items.answer: The lotus symbolizes purity, enlightenment, and rebirth across many cultures. In Buddhism, it represents spiritual awakening. In Hinduism, it's associated with divine beauty and creation. The lotus growing from muddy water to bloom in pristine beauty is a powerful metaphor for overcoming adversity.

items.question: How deep should the water be for growing lotus?
items.answer: For optimal growth, maintain 15-30 cm of water above the soil surface for most varieties. Dwarf varieties can grow in as little as 10 cm of water. The total depth including soil should be 45-75 cm. Water that is too deep may prevent leaves from reaching the surface.

items.question: Do lotus flowers come back every year?
items.answer: Yes, lotus is a perennial plant. In climates where the rhizomes don't freeze, lotus will return each spring. In colder regions, protect the rhizomes by ensuring the pond doesn't freeze solid, or store tubers in damp sand indoors over winter.

items.question: What is the lotus effect?
items.answer: The lotus effect refers to the self-cleaning property of lotus leaves. Their surface has microscopic bumps coated in wax that make water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt and debris with it. This superhydrophobic property has inspired many industrial applications, from self-cleaning paints to waterproof fabrics.

items.question: Can lotus survive in cold climates?
items.answer: Lotus can survive winter in USDA zones 4-10, provided the rhizomes don't freeze. In cold climates, ensure the pond is deep enough (at least 60 cm) so the bottom doesn't freeze. Alternatively, grow lotus in containers and move them to a frost-free location in winter.

items.question: How do I propagate lotus?
items.answer: Lotus can be propagated by dividing rhizomes in early spring or by growing from seed. Rhizome division is faster and more reliable. For seeds, nick the hard seed coat, soak in warm water until sprouting (7-14 days), then plant in soil under shallow water.
